chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked him about a man who did not know whether to trim or shave his head, so he departed from Mina. He said: Let him return to Mina so that he may shave his hair there or trim it, and upon the forehead is the shaving of the head.

key_terms.الصُّورَةِ: the forehead (specifically the center of the head where shaving is emphasized)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina (a location near Mecca where Hajj rituals occur)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they are unsure whether they shaved or trimmed their head after leaving Mina?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the precautionary measure of returning to Mina to perform the missing hair-cutting ritual when a pilgrim is uncertain between shaving (*halq*) and trimming (*taqsir*). The Imam’s directive to default to shaving underscores the principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) in completing the rites, ensuring the validity of exiting the state of *Ihram* despite the doubt. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on resolving ambiguities in ritual acts through definitive actions to secure the completeness of worship.
